stack.notes: IMPORTANT ARCHITECTURE FINDING (this is what the brief flagged: 'find where its .vue components actually live'): they mostly don't. Only 2 .vue files exist in the whole repo (app.vue = <UApp><NuxtPage/></UApp>, pages/[...slug].vue = a catch-all rendering <div id="app" />). The real UI is a pre-existing vanilla-DOM/TypeScript client under src/client/ (44 .ts files, 13101 LOC total) that self-mounts via plugins/gonogo-shell.client.ts (onNuxtReady -> dynamic import of src/client/main -> client.renderCurrentLocation(), hooked to the Nuxt router for navigation only). narduk-core/analytics/seo/mapkit-nuxt ARE real, current-version narduk-libs dependencies, registered as Nuxt modules -- but they are consumed for infrastructure (SEO meta, sitemap, mapkit token route, analytics loader) not for their Vue components (AppBreadcrumbs, AdminAnalyticsDashboard, etc. are never referenced -- there is no Vue component tree to place them in).

local_reimplementations.name: Calendar week-span grid (calendar/view.ts)
local_reimplementations.notes: Pure model-in/HTML-string-out renderer. Deliberately uses a real <table> for the weekday grid so screen readers announce the weekday column (module doc comment, lines 1-14); a per-day cell is a <button aria-expanded> that opens a detail panel, not a link.

local_reimplementations.name: Day gate-breakdown table (day/view.ts)
local_reimplementations.notes: A second real <table> (lines 140-153: thead with scope="col" Gate/Limit/Value/Result, tbody rows with scope="row"), plus a <ul class="gg-day__checklist"> source-check list. Small fixed row count (gates), no sort/paginate/search.

local_reimplementations.name: shell.ts (app chrome)
local_reimplementations.notes: Hand-rolled app shell/header, not narduk-core's LayerAppShell/LayerAppHeader despite narduk-core being an actual dependency here -- the Vue-based shell components are simply not used by this non-Vue UI.

table.notes: NON-VUE: hand-built HTML-string table via a TS renderer (escapeHtml-escaped), not a .vue SFC. Reported here because it is a genuine hand-rolled table pattern the brief asked to find regardless of framework.
NON-VUE, see above. Accessible scope="row"/scope="col" table for a per-day safety-gate breakdown.

status_chip_badge.notes: dot(tone: StatusTone) helper renders a <span class="gg-dot gg-dot--{tone}">; a verdict/tone chip, non-Vue.

notes: gonogo is a genuine architecture outlier in this lane: it has real, current narduk-libs dependencies (narduk-core 1.23.2, narduk-analytics, narduk-seo, narduk-mapkit-nuxt) wired as Nuxt modules, but its entire rendered UI is a pre-existing 13.1k-LOC vanilla-DOM/TypeScript client (src/client/, 44 files) that Nuxt only hosts and routes for -- zero Vue component tree exists for narduk-libs' Vue components to plug into. Its two hand-rolled 'tables' (calendar week grid, day gate-breakdown) are real semantic <table> elements with better accessibility (scope attributes, aria-expanded) than most Vue-based 'raw-table'/'grid-div' patterns seen elsewhere in this survey, but a Vue-based shared table component cannot be dropped in without either a Vue rewrite of these two screens or a non-Vue-consumable version of the shared table. No top_extraction_candidates are listed because nothing here is Vue-portable as-is; flag for the orchestrator as a migration-prerequisite case rather than a component-swap case.
